html:
Spanish Morocco was the part of Morocco ruled by Spain from 1912 to 1956: a strip along the Mediterranean coast and a southern zone near Cape Juby.

It was set up in 1912, when France made the rest of the country its protectorate under the Treaty of Fez and handed Spain the north. The capital was Tetouan. The Rif mountains in the north resisted. In the Rif War, Berber fighters under Abd el-Krim routed a Spanish army at Annual in 1921 and founded a Rif Republic. Spain and France together defeated it in 1926.

The colonial army raised here became a power in Spanish politics. In July 1936 Francisco Franco led it from Morocco in the rising that began the Spanish Civil War, and Moroccan troops fought for him. When French Morocco became independent in 1956, Spain handed back its northern zone too, and the southern zone in 1958. Ceuta and Melilla, never part of the protectorate, are still Spanish.
sum: Spanish Morocco was the part of Morocco ruled by Spain from 1912 to 1956: a strip along the Mediterranean coast and a southern zone near Cape Juby.
